text.p: - A number of leaders of regions in Russia's North Caucasus sent an appeal to President Yeltsin in November 1994 for consitutional order to be restored in Chechnya and this was used as an excuse for starting the war there, says Ruslan Aushev, President of the North Caucasian republic of Ingushetia. He says he was among the few who did not sign the letter.
- If a new state border law is approved by the president, anyone crossing the Russian border will have to pay a special fee.
- Russia has managed to gain a special status in relations with NATO, that is, the status of an outsider.

- The rules of the budget debate game are strict -- the government pretends it is making concessions and the State Duma lower house of parliament will have to pretend that it accepts these concessions.

- After defeating the opposition, Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko is now refraining from public statements on the Commonwealth of Independent States' future and on further integration with Russia.
- If the parliament does not approve the 1997 budget, the country's economy may be damaged, says Sergei Belyayev, head of the Duma's pro-government faction, Our Home is Russia.
- Local elections in Russia have proved that Moscow is losing power while the regions are gaining more independence.

- Looking back at the Belavezh agreement signed five years ago by Russia, Belarus and Ukraine, former Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev blames Boris Yeltsin and his team for the collapse of the Soviet Union.
